title: Security under load — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, someone proposes bypassing authorization in a benchmark. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences on what a benchmark without authorization measures, what it does not, and what you would run instead.

vocabulary.meaning: measuring the system in the configuration it actually runs in, since removing a layer measures a system nobody deploys
a component left out of a measurement, whose own cost then disappears from the reported figure

expectedElements: What the shortcut actually measures is stated
The omitted layer is identified as a real cost
A workable alternative protocol is proposed
modelAnswer: Disabling authorization would measure a configuration we never deploy. Every production request passes through that check, which itself costs a token validation and a lookup, and removing it moves that cost out of the figure we would then quote. The measurement would be real evidence for a question nobody asked. I propose running the same benchmark with a pre-issued token, which keeps the layer in place while removing the variability the proposal was trying to avoid.
commonMistakes: Rejecting the shortcut without acknowledging the noise it was meant to remove
Failing to name the omitted layer as a real cost in the reported figure
variants: Rewrite the update as the agreed benchmark protocol.
